analysis.investment_thesis: Anant Raj has done the hard work of deleveraging — borrowings fell from INR 1,691 Cr in FY20 to INR 563 Cr in FY25, and D/E now stands at a clean 0.13. But real estate is a sector I fundamentally distrust for long-term compounding, and ROE of just 10.9% confirms the business earns below my minimum threshold.
key_strengths: Dramatic debt reduction over five years: borrowings down 67% from peak, D/E now 0.13 — management has shown financial discipline
Promoter holding at 57.41% is above my threshold and gives alignment comfort
Revenue inflection is real: from INR 250 Cr in FY21 to INR 2,060 Cr in FY25, driven by real estate recovery and data centre expansion
key_risks: History is damning: profits collapsed from INR 70 Cr (FY16) to INR 9 Cr (FY21) — this is a deeply cyclical business masquerading as a growth story
ROE of 10.9% and ROCE of 11.2% are below my 15% minimum — the business does not earn enough on the capital deployed
Operating cash flow is erratic: 3 of 5 years positive, with significant negative years — typical of real estate booking recognition volatility
red_flags: Real estate sector carries inherent governance and related-party transaction risks that I am never fully comfortable with
P/E of 35x for a cyclical business with ROE of 11% is expensive — you are paying growth multiples for a cyclical
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The balance sheet cleanup is genuinely impressive — going from INR 1,691 Cr of debt in FY20 to INR 563 Cr in FY25 while growing revenue fourfold shows management intent. The data centre pivot adds an interesting dimension. But I have watched too many real estate cycles to trust this sector for a 10-year holding: the FY16–FY21 era saw profits collapse by 87% and near-zero cash generation for consecutive years.

At 35x P/E with ROE of only 10.9%, the market is pricing in sustained high growth that real estate companies rarely deliver over full cycles. My style is to buy boring, predictable businesses at sensible prices — Anant Raj is neither boring nor cheaply priced today. The promoter holding is reassuring, but it is not sufficient to overcome structural sector concerns.
